t: You're at St Giles-in-the-Fields, the parish church that gives its name to the surrounding district. The present building is the third on this site since 1101, and was rebuilt in 1731 to 1733 in Palladian style by Henry Flitcroft. It's named for St Giles the Hermit. Several writers and thinkers are buried here. The poet Andrew Marvell, a friend of John Milton, lies here, along with the translator of Homer, George Chapman. The mathematician John Pell, the physician William Watson and the poet-soldier Lord Herbert of Cherbury are also buried here.
